title: Drum Machine Designer Tricks
intro: Drum Machine Designer is a Track Stack in disguise. Every pad is a real channel strip with its own inserts, sends and automation — which means you can mix a drum kit exactly like you mix a band.

tips.t: Drag any audio file straight onto a pad
tips.d: Drop a sample onto a pad and Drum Machine Designer loads it into a Quick Sampler instance automatically. Building a custom kit takes about a minute.

tips.t: Every pad is its own channel strip
tips.d: Open the Mixer with X and you will see each pad as a separate channel inside the stack. Compress the snare, saturate the kick, send only the claps to reverb.

tips.t: ⌥‑drag a pad to copy it, including all its processing
tips.d: Copy a pad when you want to layer. Control-click the pad and choose Copy, then Control-click the pad you want to replace and choose Paste. Pitch the copy down and blend it under the original for a thicker snare. (Dragging a pad to an empty slot in the grid moves it rather than copying it, which is how you reorder a kit.)

tips.t: Use the pad's Sound tab for quick shaping
tips.d: Use the Pad Controls button for quick shaping. Select a pad and click Pad Controls in the bar below the grid: the pad's tone and effect Smart Controls appear in the Plug-in pane, so you can reshape a kit piece without going into its plug-in. When you do need the sample itself — playback mode, sample start, the pitch, filter and amp envelopes — the same bar has Q-Sampler Main, Q-Sampler Details or Drum Synth buttons that open that pad's instrument right below the grid.

tips.t: Use the main stack fader for the whole kit
tips.d: The Track Stack's top level is a summing bus. Put your kit compressor and limiter there and process everything together.

tips.t: Save your kit as a patch
tips.d: With the stack selected, save to the Library. Every pad, every sample and every insert comes back in one click on the next project.
